title: Nonlinear parabolic compactness and monotone evolution

items.title: Banach evolution triples and weak time derivatives
items.statement: Define a real reflexive Banach evolution triple V densely and continuously embedded in a real Hilbert space H, the canonical embedding H→V*, Bochner Lp(V) and Lp′(V*) classes, distributional time derivative, and the trace convention used in PE12.
items.strategy: Extend the published Hilbert evolution-triple convention to a separable reflexive Banach energy space and specify every pairing and weak derivative.

items.title: Coercive monotone p-growth diffusion fluxes
items.statement: For bounded C1 Ω⊂R^d, d≥2, and p>max(1,2d/(d+2)), define the Carathéodory flux a(x,ξ), its induced map A:W0^{1,p}(Ω)→W0^{1,p}(Ω)*, p-growth, coercivity, monotonicity, and continuity assumptions.
items.strategy: State the exact pointwise hypotheses that make the variational flux well-defined, p-growth bounded, coercive and monotone.

items.title: Conforming FEM families with stable L2 projectors
items.statement: Define finite-dimensional conforming spaces Vh⊂V with H-orthogonal projections Πh that are uniformly bounded V→V, converge strongly to the identity on V and H, and are paired with time partitions whose maximum step tends to zero.
items.strategy: Make the exact spatial projection and mesh-density interface used to lift the finite-dimensional time derivative into V* explicit.

items.title: The subcritical W0^{1,p} embedding into L2
items.statement: For bounded C1 Ω⊂R^d, d≥1, and p>max(1,2d/(d+2)), W0^{1,p}(Ω) embeds continuously and compactly into L2(Ω).
items.strategy: Split p<d from p≥d; use the exact strict subcritical exponent in the first branch and finite-measure Lp-to-L2 continuity after Rellich in the second.

items.title: Time translations and mollification in Bochner Lp
items.statement: For a strongly measurable Banach-valued f∈Lp(0,T;X), 1≤p<∞, local time translations are continuous in Lp and scalar time mollifiers converge to f in Lp on compact subintervals; interval averages on partitions with vanishing maximum step converge in Lp.
items.strategy: Approximate by finite-valued simple functions, use scalar Lp translation continuity componentwise, then Minkowski and density.

items.title: The zero-boundary W1p space is separable and reflexive
items.statement: Assume the ultrafilter lemma, Dependent Choice and Hahn–Banach. If Ω⊂R^d is bounded and open, d≥1, and 1<p<∞, then W0^{1,p}(Ω), with its inherited W1p norm, is a separable reflexive real Banach space.
items.strategy: Use the closed-subspace theorem for reflexivity; embed W1p isometrically into a finite product of Lp spaces, restrict rational box-step approximants, then use a countable base to obtain separability of its subspace W0p.

items.title: Bochner Lp is complete for a Banach value space
items.statement: For a real Banach space X, finite T, and 1≤p<∞, the Bochner space Lp(0,T;X) with its integral norm is complete.
items.strategy: Choose a rapidly Cauchy subsequence, sum the pointwise norms of its increments, use monotone convergence to obtain an almost-everywhere Cauchy series, and estimate its Lp tail by Minkowski.

references.title: Tomáš Roubíček, Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations with Applications, 2nd ed., Birkhäuser, 2005
references.locator: §1.5, Bochner spaces and their completeness

items.title: The Banach evolution-space energy identity and H trace
items.statement: If u∈Lp(0,T;V), u′∈Lp′(0,T;V*) with 1<p<∞ in a Banach evolution triple, then u has a unique representative in C([0,T];H) and satisfies the integrated Hilbert norm chain rule.
items.strategy: Mollify on interior intervals, pass the scalar norm derivative to L1, then use scalar pairings, density of V in H, Riesz representation and norm continuity to construct the strong H trace.

items.title: Aubin–Lions compactness with exact time exponent
items.statement: If V⊂H⊂V* with V compactly embedded in H and continuously embedded in V*, a family bounded in Lp(0,T;V) with distributional derivative bounded in Lq(0,T;V*), 1<p<∞ and 1<q≤∞, is relatively compact in Lp(0,T;H). With a uniform L∞(0,T;H) bound the same subsequence converges strongly in every finite Lr(0,T;H).
items.strategy: Approximate the V unit ball by finite-dimensional H subspaces, control coefficients by the V* derivative, use finite-dimensional equicontinuity and send the H approximation error to zero.

items.title: Piecewise-constant discrete Aubin–Lions compactness
items.statement: For conforming-space-valued piecewise-constant reconstructions on partitions with maximum step δk→0, uniform Lp(V) and piecewise discrete derivative Lq(V*) bounds with q>1 imply relative compactness in Lp(H); the time-translate bound is O(h+δk), and a uniform L∞(H) bound upgrades convergence to every finite Lr(H).
items.strategy: Compare the piecewise-constant reconstruction with its affine interpolant, prove an O(δk) reconstruction defect and O(h+δk) V* translates, then use the same finite-rank compact approximation.

items.title: An outward-pointing finite-dimensional map has a zero
items.statement: If F:R^N→R^N is continuous and F(x)·x>0 on a sphere of radius R, then F has a zero in the closed ball.
items.strategy: Normalize −F on the ball to obtain a Brouwer fixed point; a fixed point must lie on the sphere and contradict the outward-pointing inequality.

items.title: Backward Euler monotone Galerkin steps and energy bounds
items.statement: For each finite-dimensional conforming Vh and time step, a continuous coercive monotone p-growth flux admits a backward Euler Galerkin solution; testing by the new value yields uniform L∞(H), Lp(V), jump-energy and discrete derivative bounds.
items.strategy: Apply the outward-pointing Brouwer lemma at each step, test with the new solution, use the Hilbert discrete energy identity, coercivity and conjugate-exponent Young inequality.

items.title: Weak limits of bounded space-time Sobolev gradients
items.statement: For bounded C1 Ω, finite T and 1<p<∞, any sequence bounded in Lp(0,T;W0^{1,p}(Ω)) has a subsequence whose zero extensions and all spatial weak derivatives converge weakly in scalar Lp((0,T)×R^d), with the limit still in Lp(0,T;W0^{1,p}(Ω)).
items.strategy: Embed the zero-extended function and its spatial gradient into a finite product of scalar Lp spaces, extract a weak limit, pass the distributional derivative identity, and recover zero trace on the C1 boundary.

items.title: Minty identification for monotone diffusion fluxes
items.statement: Let a(x,ξ) be a Carathéodory monotone flux with p-growth. If gradients converge weakly in Lp(Q), fluxes converge weakly in Lp′(Q), and the flux-gradient pairings satisfy the Minty limsup inequality, then the weak flux limit equals a(x,∇u).
items.strategy: Integrate the pointwise monotonicity inequality against arbitrary comparison gradients, pass to the limsup, then test with ∇u±ε∇w and use dominated convergence and hemicontinuity.

items.title: Backward Euler FEM subsequential convergence to a monotone weak solution
items.statement: Under the flux hypotheses, the subcritical W0^{1,p}→L2 embedding, and the explicitly defined conforming FEM family with uniformly V-stable L2 projectors, backward Euler reconstructions have a subsequence converging strongly in L2(0,T;L2), weakly in space-time W0^{1,p}, and whose flux limit is identified by Minty as a weak solution; monotonicity gives uniqueness.
items.strategy: Use the energy bound, projected discrete derivative estimate and discrete Aubin–Lions compactness; pass the weak equation and initial trace, derive the Minty limsup from the discrete energy identity, identify the flux, and prove uniqueness by the chain rule.

items.title: Quantitative residual error under strong monotonicity
items.statement: For two weak evolution fields with residual difference R and identical diffusion, if A is strongly monotone with exponent p, the H-time error and the Lp(V) error are bounded by the initial H error and the Lp′(V*) residual norm.
items.strategy: Subtract the weak equations, test by the solution difference, apply the energy chain rule and p/p′ Young inequality, then integrate.

title: Nonlinear parabolic compactness and monotone evolution — Examples

items.title: The p-Laplacian is an admissible monotone diffusion
items.statement: For p>max(1,2d/(d+2)), the flux a(ξ)=|ξ|^{p−2}ξ satisfies the monotonicity and p-growth hypotheses and its zero-boundary space embeds compactly in L2; the conditional FEM convergence theorem therefore applies when the projector interface is met.
items.strategy: Identify a as the gradient of the convex function |ξ|^p/p, verify its growth and coercivity, and invoke the proved Sobolev embedding and convergence theorem.

items.title: A Barenblatt profile has finite propagation
items.statement: For m>1, the one-dimensional porous-medium equation u_t=(u^m)_{xx} admits an explicit nonnegative profile with compact support at every positive time and interface radius proportional to t^{1/(m+1)}.
items.strategy: Differentiate the positive-part self-similar profile in its positivity region, match the scaling exponents and coefficient, then verify the flux has no boundary delta and compute the support.

items.title: The linear Ritz projection need not commute with the p-Laplacian
items.statement: The assertion that the linear Laplace Ritz projection preserves the nonlinear p-Laplace Galerkin residual for every input is false.
items.strategy: Use Ω=(0,1), the two-element P1 space, u(x)=x(1−x) and p=3; compute both residual pairings against the midpoint hat function and compare 1/2 with 2/3.

items.title: Time oscillations defeat compactness without derivative control
items.statement: A bounded family in L2(0,T;V) can fail to be relatively compact in L2(0,T;H) when no positive-exponent V* time-derivative or translate bound is imposed.
items.strategy: Take distinct integer temporal frequencies multiplying one fixed nonzero V vector; orthogonality gives a uniform positive pairwise L2(H) distance while the L2(V) norms stay constant.
